title: State of Kerala v. Jolly Joseph (Koodathayi Serial Cyanide Poisonings)
crime_type: Serial Familial Poisoning / Inheritance Homicide / Forgery
court_or_authority: High Court of Kerala / Principal District & Sessions Court, Kozhikode
legal_citation: Bail Application No. 1544/2020; Sessions Case No. 81/2020 (Kozhikode)
source: High Court of Kerala Case Status Records & Indian Kanoon (doc/182573273)
ipc_sections: Section 468 IPC (Forgery for purpose of cheating)
Section 471 IPC (Using forged document as genuine)
evidence: Exhumation of six remains from church cemetery vaults across Koodathayi and chemical toxicological identification
Forensic laboratory confirmation of cyanide trace residue in soil and bone matter of Roy Thomas
Forged last will and testament of father-in-law Tom Thomas fabricated to divert ancestral estate ownership
Recovery of cyanide container concealed in cattle shed at suspect's residence based on disclosure statement under Section 27 Evidence Act
Digital mobile call history and financial transfers between accused and cyanide procurement contacts
modus_operandi: Systematically eliminated six family members across a 14-year span (2002 to 2016) including mother-in-law, father-in-law, husband, maternal uncle, and a two-year-old child. Mixed minute lethal doses of potassium cyanide obtained from a goldsmith into customary food preparations (mutton soup, mushroom curry, water). Fabricated medical narratives of sudden cardiac arrest or choking to avoid autopsy.
personality_disorder: Forensic psychiatric evaluations documented high-functioning sociopathic traits, pathological compartmentalization, duplicity (posing as an NIT Calicut lecturer for 14 years), and calculating avarice.
common_traits: Targeting close family and marital relatives over extended intervals
Posing as reputable, devout, and respectable community member
Use of kitchen food substances as vehicle for chemical cyanide
Prevention of post-mortem examinations by citing cultural/religious reservations
Fabrication of property documentation and wills to seize assets
summary: Extraordinary Kerala serial homicide investigation involving six poisoning deaths between 2002 and 2016 within a single household. Unraveled after the NRI son initiated inquiries into the fraudulent transfer of ancestral estate, leading to exhumation of remains and multi-agency forensic indictment.
